clue.text: Mushroom with squid, the best recipe out?

indicators.note: out tells the solver to throw something away, here the abbreviation that recipe stands for

blocks.note: in underwater hockey the weighted puck is called a squid
the best is the first, as in first-rate
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, take)

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether a mushroom-and-squid dish is the finest recipe going.
explanation.walkthrough: Squid looks like the seafood but is the name for the weighted puck in underwater hockey (octopush), a little-known sport. R is the standard prescription abbreviation for recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Puckfist is an old dialect name for the puffball, a round fungus that bursts into dusty spores.

clue.text: Shell out spending last penny on return trip

indicators.note: spending its last means using up the final letter, so that letter goes
a return trip goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: someone out is away from home
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A traveller pays out their final penny on a journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell out' reads as paying money; Shell is the definition, and out is the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paua or pawa is the Maori name for the abalone, a sea snail with an iridescent shell.

clue.text: I'll pick up as I settled that old fight

blocks.note: ut is Latin for as, found in Chambers
taken as written
a bird that has lit on a branch has settled there
yt is an old written abbreviation for that, with y standing for the letter thorn
a ruck is a scuffle or fight

explanation.surface: Someone vows to resume an old quarrel as they settle up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll pick up' sounds like a person speaking; read the vehicle as the speaker, a pickup.
explanation.definitionFit: A utility truck is a small open-backed vehicle, the pickup, which collects and carries loads.

clue.text: International player entertaining league by way of defensive device

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one word holds another

blocks.note: a player who has represented their country is a cap
L is the abbreviation for league
thro is a shortened spelling of through, meaning via

explanation.surface: A footballer for his country hosts a league side using a defensive system.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap is awarded for each appearance for a national team, so an international player is a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A calthrop (caltrop) is a spiked iron device strewn on the ground to lame horses or stop vehicles.

clue.text: Worried about Thailand and Zambia involved in terrible feud

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters come out of order
involved in means wrapped up inside, so the two letters go within the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

explanation.surface: Diplomats fret about two countries caught up in a bitter dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To futz is American slang for fiddling or messing aimlessly, which fits fretting at something.

clue.text: I can blame blundering on small discrepancies

indicators.note: blundering moves clumsily and carelessly, scattering the letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An accountant blames slips for minor gaps in the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbalances are inequalities between quantities, and discrepancies are mismatches between figures.

clue.text: I appreciate that fast ability

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thank you
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone thanks another for a quick turn of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast reads as quick, but it is the religious fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural aptitude or skill, a synonym of ability.

clue.text: Stubborn sort's reason to get the hell out

indicators.note: getting something out means removing it from the word it sits in

blocks.note: to reason with someone is to discuss things
Dis is the classical underworld, i.e. hell

explanation.surface: Someone obstinate has a motive for clearing off in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'get the hell out' reads as slang for leaving; in fact Dis, the underworld, is being taken out of a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuss is an informal word for a person, especially an awkward or perverse character.

clue.text: Onset of coronary left aircraftman in office job

definitions.note: the answer is a person who does such a job

indicators.note: the onset of anything is its beginning, so its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of coronary
L is the abbreviation for left
erk is RAF slang for a lowest-ranked aircraftman

explanation.surface: An airman suffers a heart attack while working at a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: An erk is British forces slang for a lowly aircraftman or rating.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk is an office worker who keeps records, so the clue loosely names the person by the post.

clue.text: Quickly dropping Beefy when admitting hoo-ha

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word takes the other inside

blocks.note: a beefy person is big and strapping
a hoo-ha is a fuss, an ado

explanation.surface: Beefy, a nickname of cricketer Ian Botham, falling suddenly amid a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefy reads as a name (Ian Botham's nickname) but is just the adjective. The definition is grim: strappado was torture by hoisting a victim on a rope and letting them fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Strappadoing is subjecting someone to the strappado, a sudden drop on a rope, hence a quick dropping.

clue.text: Start to stay out more? Not guilty!

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of stay
the final Not works on both words: not out is in, not more is less

explanation.surface: A wife's suggestion to stay out more meets the indignant reply of an innocent party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Not' at the end negates both 'out' and 'more', giving their opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sinless means being free of sin, i.e. not guilty of any wrongdoing.

clue.text: Bombay duck's fate in Mumbai when out of form

indicators.note: being out of form means losing shape, so the city's letters lose their order
in puts one word inside the other, the fate sitting within the jumbled city

blocks.note: the city's name taken as written, to be jumbled
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A question of what happens to a fish called Bombay duck in its home city when it is off form.
explanation.walkthrough: Bombay duck is not a duck but a small dried fish; Mumbai is Bombay's current name, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bummalo or bummaloti is the Indian lizardfish, sold dried and salted as Bombay duck.

clue.text: Decline to discard jack going after West

indicators.note: going means departing, so the card named beside it leaves the word
after places the trimmed word behind the compass point

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for West
to jilt a lover is to discard them
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A card player declines to throw away a jack after West has played.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and West read as bridge or whist talk; here they are just abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To wilt is to droop or weaken, so it means to decline in vigour.

clue.text: Conservative beset by shivering as he reads what's on sensational front pages?

indicators.note: shivering makes things shake and tremble out of place
beset by means surrounded by, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician trembles as he reads the scandalous tabloid front pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Scareheads are huge alarming headlines, the kind splashed across tabloid front pages.

clue.text: Unproductive investing tip from Reader's Digest

indicators.note: a tip is the very end of something, here the opening letter of the magazine's word
investing means clothing or surrounding, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: lean years are unproductive ones
the first letter of Reader's

explanation.walkthrough: Reader's Digest looks like the magazine title, but Digest is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to absorb and take it in, which is what learning means.

clue.text: Spanish highness dancing late with Margherita perhaps

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
za is slang for pizza, and Margherita is one kind

explanation.surface: A Spanish royal dances into the night alongside someone called Margherita.
explanation.walkthrough: Margherita looks like a woman's name but is the classic tomato-and-mozzarella pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: Alteza is the Spanish form of address equivalent to Highness for royalty.

clue.text: Porridge is one being broadcast in instalments

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so go by the sound

blocks.note: a story published in instalments is a serial

explanation.surface: The British sitcom Porridge is being shown in instalments on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge was a BBC prison sitcom, which makes 'broadcast in instalments' feel natural; here it is just oat porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is made from oats, a grain, so it is an example of a cereal.

clue.text: Love yielding to tone in stringed instrument (guitar)

indicators.note: yielding to means giving up a place for another, so one letter makes way for a word

blocks.note: a viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a tone of colour is a hue

explanation.surface: Love gives way to a particular sound quality in a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed guitar is the definition; the stringed instrument in front of it is the one being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: The vihuela is a Renaissance Spanish instrument of the guitar family with paired strings.

clue.text: After closure of Barclays banks are finally gone, a blow to locals

indicators.note: the closure of something is its end, so its final letter
finally gone means the end has disappeared, so the last letter goes
after places the banks behind the single letter

blocks.note: the last letter of Barclays
asar is a plural of os, a glacial ridge or esker
taken as written, then trimmed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Locals lose their Barclays branch when it closes, a heavy blow to the community.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks suggests Barclays branches but means ridges: asar, plural of os. 'To locals' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasarara is a Scots dialect word for a severe scolding or a blow.

clue.text: Inability to eat a half haggis wrapped in plant

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two halves, here the front
wrapped in means enclosed by, so one piece sits inside the plant

blocks.note: taken as written
pia is a Polynesian plant, the Tahiti arrowroot
the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Someone can only face half a haggis, served wrapped in greens.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is a Scottish dish of offal cooked in a sheep's stomach, which suits the surface of not being able to eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphagia is the medical term for an inability or refusal to swallow food.

clue.text: Drama school right to cut short monologues, they'll catch those going too fast

definitions.text: they'll catch those going too fast

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the little word drops its final letter

blocks.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written, then trimmed
a rap is a spoken performance or lengthy talk

explanation.surface: Drama students are told to keep their monologues brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar traps use radar to measure speed and catch motorists who break the limit.

clue.text: Formation of pus, a little yellow and seeping so badly

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small piece of it, its opening letter
badly arranged letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: the first letter of yellow
taken as written, to be jumbled with the letter before

explanation.surface: A wound oozing nastily with a yellowish discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyogenesis is the medical term for pus formation, from Greek pyon, pus, and genesis, origin.

clue.text: To contain old men fighting, marine moves in

indicators.note: fighting men are thrown about in a melee and out of order
moves in means enters, so one piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
marine means of the sea

explanation.surface: A marine wades in to break up old soldiers brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: Old is part of the definition, flagging an obsolete word; marine reads as a soldier but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Enseam is an obsolete verb meaning to include or hold together, as in a seam.

clue.text: Numpties after seconds is cheeky

indicators.note: after places the fools behind the single letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
a numpty is Scottish slang for an idiot, an ass

explanation.surface: Idiots following on from their elders are being impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: Numpty is Scottish slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To sass someone is American informal for talking back cheekily, so sasses is cheek in verb form.

clue.text: Pollute river discharging foul material

blocks.note: taken as written
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.walkthrough: Discharging and foul fit a pollution story; foul material looks like the definition, but foul is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine netted fabric used for veils and tutus, a kind of material.

clue.text: Made no money backing Cinderella pantomime

taken as written
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.walkthrough: Cinderella is a staple of British Christmas pantomime, which disguises her role here as a char, a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a mimed party game, and a pantomime in the old sense is acting out by gesture alone.

clue.text: Men in East London are around fire

clue.text: French fiddler arranged score before start of concerto

the start of a word is its opening letter
before puts the jumbled word ahead of the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
the first letter of concerto

explanation.walkthrough: Fiddler and score suggest a violinist; fiddler is a swindler, and escroc is the French word for one.

the number written as a word

clue.text: I see favourite's last, heading for local butcher's after losing Grand National!

the final letter of favourite
the first letter of local
